subject.title: RFC: OpenShell session workers and local inference

question: Should OpenClaw adopt generic core contracts for worker-local inference, provider-authenticated SSH, and persisted per-lease routes to support this OpenShell integration?
rationale: The RFC intentionally adds permanent core API and security-boundary surface; implementation quality cannot determine whether that product and compatibility commitment is desired.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow RFC contract
options.body: Accept the proposed provider-neutral seams, subject to explicit compatibility wording and live credential-boundary proof before the companion implementation is reviewed for merge.

options.title: Keep OpenShell sandbox-only
options.body: Retain the existing plugin sandbox capability and defer worker placement plus local inference until maintainers want a broader worker-provider contract.

options.title: Request a smaller RFC
options.body: Limit the proposal to one contract, such as worker placement, and defer local inference and authenticated SSH transport to separately approved RFCs.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow RFC contract
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed provider-neutral seams, subject to explicit compatibility wording and live credential-boundary proof before the companion implementation is reviewed for merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied material identifies this author as the only concrete owner of the proposed RFC and companion implementation; an approving repository decision-maker is not identified.
